run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T08:48:34Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for frontend-proxy is backed by real error telemetry: frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans carried STATUS_CODE_ERROR (≈818 errors over the 16m ending 09:04:34) and every inspected error span was an HTTP 504 whose duration was ~15.0s, with its 'router frontend egress' child span lasting the same ~15s. Whole-trace evidence shows the proxy's upstream (frontend) took ~15s to answer a cart-page request, so the proxy's 15s timeout produced the 504. The slowness is confined to the cart path: frontend page-level GET/POST spans and its grpc CartService/AddItem and CartService/GetCart client spans exceeded 10s while its other routes and product-catalog/ad/recommendation calls stayed fast (75µs–2ms). The deepest supported finding is inside cart: every cart server span in the window is an error (AddItem 45.2, GetCart 38.8 increases, 0 non-error spans) and every cart GetCart error span was longer than 15000ms, while cart's pod logs record repeated 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' from 08:48:53, and cart's only redis endpoint is VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379. So the alert is a downstream symptom of cart losing its redis dependency (valkey-cart). Why valkey-cart would not accept connections is NOT established: the valkey-cart pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, its Service endpoints point at it, its CPU/memory are flat with zero memory-limit hits, and it defines no readiness or liveness probe, so 'Ready' proves nothing about redis serving. A network-level block between cart and valkey-cart and an internal redis stall remain separate, unresolved hypotheses. Errors started at ~08:48 (matching the alert start) and had returned to 0 by the 5m window ending 09:01:34.

claims.text: frontend-proxy error spans are concentrated on the 'ingress' operation: over the 16m window ending 2026-11-17T09:04:34Z the increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy"} was 817.94 spans with status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR and 2031.83 with STATUS_CODE_UNSET for span_name="ingress", while span_name="router frontend egress" had 0 error spans.

In the 16m window ending 09:04:34Z, the largest per-service error-span increase was frontend-proxy 'ingress' 817.94; other services with error spans included frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem' 46.31, 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' 32.30, 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart' 81.27, 'POST /api/checkout' 7.29; cart 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem' 45.23 and 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' 38.77; checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 6.75 and 'oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' 6.75.

The alert onset matches the telemetry: 5-minute increases of frontend-proxy ingress error spans were 0 from 07:48:34Z through 08:47:34Z, rose to 53.33 at the window ending 08:48:34Z (the alert start), peaked at ~438 per 5m, and were 0 again at the window ending 09:01:34Z.

frontend-proxy error spans are 504s at a fixed 15s: rows shown include frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans with status_tags error=true, http.status_code="504", otel.status_code="ERROR" and durations 14,999,635–15,001,202 µs, each with a 'router frontend egress' child of the same ~15.0s carrying http.status_code="0".

Whole trace a545ba7815ee3f559a6bbcc06809bf79 shows the mechanism: load-generator 'user_view_cart' 15.003s, load-generator GET 15.003s with http.status_code="504", frontend-proxy ingress 15.001s with 504, router frontend egress 15.001s, and a frontend GET span of 14.999s that itself recorded http.status_code="200" — i.e. the proxy timed out waiting on the frontend, not the reverse.

Slowness is confined to the cart path inside frontend: counting spans over 10000ms in the 16m window, frontend spans were GET 227.15, POST 591.83, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 46.31, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 32.30, while GET /, GET /api/data, GET /api/recommendations, GET /api/products/{productId}, grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations were all 0.

cart is failing entirely during the window: 16m increases for cart server spans were 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem' STATUS_CODE_ERROR 45.23 with STATUS_CODE_UNSET 0, and 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' STATUS_CODE_ERROR 38.77 with STATUS_CODE_UNSET 0, and cart's redis client spans (HGET, HMSET, EXPIRE) and its flagd ResolveBoolean client span all show 0 increases.

Every cart GetCart error span exceeded 15s: for span_name="POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart", status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR, the 16m increase is 38.77 in bucket le="+Inf" and 0 in every bucket up to and including le="15000.0"; cart spans above 1000ms were AddItem 45.23 and GetCart 38.77, matching its error counts exactly.

cart's pod logs name the failing dependency: from 08:48:53Z onward the cart container alternately logs 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' and 'Error status code '{StatusCode}' with detail '{Detail}' raised.' between GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync request lines; the newest cart log line available is 2026-11-17T08:55:10.5389067Z.
The redis endpoint cart is configured to use is service valkey-cart port 6379: the cart Deployment container env contains VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379 (alongside FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013).

The valkey-cart object is present and wired: Service valkey-cart is ClusterIP 100.68.233.28 with port 6379 and selector opentelemetry.io/name=valkey-cart, and its Endpoints resolve to address 100.96.2.228 on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae with targetRef Pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr, port 6379.

The valkey-cart Deployment runs image valkey/valkey:8.1.3-alpine with container port 6379, resources limits cpu=10m memory=10Mi (requests 2m/4Mi), and defines no readinessProbe and no livenessProbe; its pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr is Running with Ready=true and restartCount 0.

valkey-cart itself shows no resource failure in the window: its container CPU rate stayed ~0.002–0.0034 cores (baseline ~0.002–0.0025) and its working set stayed ~7.6–8.6MB with container_memory_failcnt = 0 at every sampled point through 09:00:34Z.

The cart path was clean before the burst: in the 16m window ending 08:46:00Z, frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' error increase was 0, frontend 'POST' and 'GET /api/cart' error increases were 0, and no cart error series were returned for that window, while frontend-proxy ingress had only 7.23 background errors.

Non-cart paths were fast in the same window: in the 08:49:30–08:51:30Z frontend trace sample, product-catalog 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' spans were 75–161µs, ad 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' 687–1221µs, recommendation '/oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations' 1958µs, and frontend 'GET /api/products/{productId}' 1873–43558µs with http.status_code 200, while cart-path requests (load-generator user_view_cart 15.003s and user_add_to_cart 15.009s) ended in 504.

All 5 nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False and PIDPressure=False, and all 21 otel-demo pods are Running/Ready with restartCount 0, so no pod on this cluster shows a crash, OOMKill or node-pressure signature.

Long-running, pre-existing noise is present but separate from this cause: events in namespace otel-demo contain only two groups, both about the OLD pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s — 75 Normal 'Killing' events ('Stopping container cart', first 2026-11-15T19:47:58Z, last 2026-11-17T08:51:24Z) and 30 Warning 'FailedKillPod' events (fail to KillContainer/KillPodSandbox, context deadline exceeded, last 08:51:24Z); that pod is on node i-00702f4ac4662cf00 and is not in the cart Service endpoints (which list only cart-755465879b-t9mf7 at 100.96.2.233).

The flagd feature-flag ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) as read now defines 12 flags — adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure — all with defaultVariant "off"; the object carries no timestamp for its earlier content.

frontend was not resource-starved while hanging: its container CPU-throttled-periods rate fell from ~4.9–6.9/s before the burst to ~1.4–1.6/s during it, i.e. the frontend was idle waiting on the cart call rather than CPU-throttled.

Rejected: that the alert reflects a general platform/node-wide slowdown. Nodes report no pressure and all pods are Ready with 0 restarts, and product-catalog/ad/recommendation calls plus frontend non-cart routes stayed in the sub-millisecond to tens-of-milliseconds range while only cart-path requests hit 15s timeouts.

Rejected: that the stuck terminating pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s caused the cart failures. Its Killing/FailedKillPod events predate the incident (first 2026-11-15T19:47:58Z), it lives on node i-00702f4ac4662cf00 (not the node hosting cart, valkey-cart or frontend-proxy), it holds a flat ~29MB working set with no CPU use, and the cart Service routes only to cart-755465879b-t9mf7.

Likely causal chain (supported at each step by the telemetry above, but the redis-side fault is not directly observed): the valkey-cart redis endpoint stopped serving cart, cart logged 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' and every CartService call hung past 15s, frontend's cart-page requests consequently exceeded the frontend-proxy 15s upstream timeout, and frontend-proxy returned 504s that drove the RequestErrorRate alert.

Open hypothesis A: connectivity between the cart pod (100.96.2.233) and the valkey-cart pod (100.96.2.228 on the same node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae) was blocked or blackholed around 08:48–08:59Z (e.g. a temporary network policy or chaos-style network fault). This would explain connection failures lasting ~11 minutes while the valkey container kept running with normal CPU/memory and zero restarts, but no network metric or policy object in this Run shows such a block.

Open hypothesis B: the valkey-cart container itself stopped accepting client connections (internal stall or exhausted client handling) while its process kept running; the Deployment defines no readinessProbe, so the pod's Ready=True cannot be read as proof that redis served port 6379, and its container logs returned no lines to confirm or deny an internal error.

Open hypothesis C: cart's own saturation amplified the outage — cart's CPU-throttled-periods rate rose from ~1.0/s to 6.9–8.9/s and its working set from ~120MB to ~187MB in the same 2-minute samples as the error burst, which is consistent with blocked redis connection attempts piling up worker threads, but these samples rise with the burst rather than clearly before it, so precedence is undetermined.

Add a readinessProbe and livenessProbe to the valkey-cart Deployment (e.g. redis PING on port 6379) so that a redis instance which is running but not serving stops being reported Ready and stops receiving Service traffic.

On the redis side, inspect valkey-cart connection counts, maxclients, blocked clients and slowlog for 08:45–09:05Z, and check calico/cilium or chaos tooling for a network rule or experiment scoped to cart or valkey-cart at 08:48Z; this is the missing evidence needed to choose between hypothesis A and hypothesis B.

Separately from this alert, clean up the long-stuck old pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s on node i-00702f4ac4662cf00, whose container the kubelet has repeatedly failed to kill since 2026-11-15T19:47:58Z (FailedKillPod / DeadlineExceeded); it is not part of this incident but indicates an unhealthy container-runtime state for that container.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not visible: list_prometheus_rules returned no rules both with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and unfiltered, so its expression (and the annotation value 1.0888) could not be verified against the metrics read here.
No change-history integration is available in this Run, so a change, restart or chaos experiment affecting cart or valkey-cart at ~08:48Z cannot be confirmed or excluded.

The valkey-cart container's logs returned no lines for 08:40–09:04Z, and redis exposes no metrics in this target, so the internal state of valkey-cart (accepting connections, maxclients, blocking) at the time of the failure is unknown.
The valkey-cart Deployment has no readiness/liveness probe, so its Ready=True condition does not demonstrate that port 6379 was served.
The networkpolicies query for namespace otel-demo returned no rows at query time; whether any policy existed during the incident window is unknown, and it is not evidence that none existed then.
Metrics named kube_* returned nothing from this Prometheus, so kube-state-metrics history (pod restarts, pod owner, container restarts over time) was unavailable for the window.

Traces are a biased, sampled view: traces_search for service cart returned no traces in 08:50–08:52Z and error=true / otel.status_code="ERROR" tag searches returned nothing even though the span metrics show cart and frontend cart-call error spans, so the per-span call graph for the hanging requests is only partially known.

cart's newest available log line is 08:55:10Z while ingress errors continued until roughly 08:59Z; whether cart stopped logging, stopped accepting connections, or the log stream was truncated in that interval is unknown.

The flagd flag values during the incident window are unknown: the ConfigMap read is as-of-now state (all defaultVariant off) and carries no timestamp, so a flag-driven fault at 08:48Z can be neither supported nor ruled out by it.
No Redis or TCP connection-level evidence exists in this Run to distinguish a network block between cart and valkey-cart from an internal redis stall.
next_steps: Pull valkey-cart redis-side telemetry for 08:45–09:05Z (connected_clients, blocked_clients, rejected_connections, maxclients, slowlog, and container stdout/stderr) to determine whether redis refused or dropped connections.

Inspect cloud/CNI and chaos experiment records for 2026-11-17T08:48Z scoped to namespace otel-demo pods cart-755465879b-t9mf7 or valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr (temporary NetworkPolicy, iptables/eBPF drop rules, or chaos-mesh network partitions).
Confirm the frontend-proxy upstream timeout (observed as 15.0s on all 504s) and decide whether cart-page requests should fail fast instead of holding the proxy open for the full timeout.
Add readiness/liveness probes to valkey-cart and a redis connectivity alert, then re-run the same cart-path latency check to establish a post-fix baseline.
Have the platform team investigate the unkillable container of pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s on node i-00702f4ac4662cf00 (repeated FailedKillPod since 2026-11-15).
